_note: Intra-Germanic blend (Anglo-Saxon + Frankish): an eastern-Frankish / Austrasian-flavored realm (homeland Ostraclia, 'the east-land') ruling older Anglo-Saxon shires. Backbone = Frankish/OHG (phonology, comites/duces feudal ladder); overlay = Anglo-Saxon (the Aetheling, ealdor-thegn forms and OE place-words in the eastern shires). civ = feudal. Even split Lawful/Neutral. Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Frankish/OE register (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are the Frankish-branch reflexes (with Anglo-Saxon-overlay variants) of the common-Germanic theonym ancestors (family_germanic.json), phoneme-morphs of the Agrippan canon, never real Germanic gods.

phonology.palette: Frankish/OHG backbone (High German shift th>d, d>t, k>ch/hh; w>w/wu; -o/-i) with Anglo-Saxon overlay touches (w-, th retained, weak -a; OE place-words); theophoric stems are the Frankish reflexes (Dulro-, Erlant-, Giando-) with AS variants (Thulor-, Eorland-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC and clusters (st, sk, pf, hh, cw); root-initial stress.

morphology.patronymic_form: patronymic -ing (descendant of); inherited lineage (kunni) for nobility; AS-overlay -ing/-sunu in the eastern shires; clergy a Latinate -us form.
morphology.compounding_rule: [adjective|resource](stem) + feature: Ostwald (east-forest), Isarnburg (iron-fort); lineage + -ingen; AS-overlay -tun/-ham for steads.

title_ladder.government: feudal (an eastern-Frankish/Austrasian realm; comites and duces under the crown, with Anglo-Saxon ealdor-thegn forms in the older shires)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Frankish feudal backbone, ascending, with Anglo-Saxon overlay at the noble tiers. Thegn (retainer-lord, AS) barony; Markigravo (margrave) march; Gravo (count) county; Herizogo (duke) duchy; Aetheling (throne-worthy prince, AS) principality; Kuning (king) kingdom; Keisar (emperor < Caesar) empire. (Rank titles are the real Frankish/OE register, allowed.)

people_name_convention.order: personal + lineage (-ing / kunni); nobility use the dynastic -ing name; the eastern shire-folk keep Anglo-Saxon names; clergy a Latinate -us form.
people_name_convention.dual_register: Frankish nobility use dithematic dynastic names; the eastern shires keep Anglo-Saxon names; clergy Latinate.
people_name_convention.theophoric: names from the Frankish deity-reflexes (with AS-overlay variants) + an element: -berht (bright), -ward (guard), -frid (peace): e.g. Dulro-berht, Eorland-ward (AS overlay).

religion._note: Deity-names are the Frankish-branch reflexes of the common-Germanic theonym ancestors (family_germanic.json), with Anglo-Saxon-overlay variants in the eastern shires - phoneme-morphs of the Agrippan canon, never real Germanic gods. Lawful/Neutral henotheist: the One above His ministers; Neutral folk keep the saints and the hallowed dead at the minster.
religion.the_one: Aiterno (< *Aiternaz < Aeternus; God on high; the AS shires say Aetern)
religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the opposing powers keep their reflexes + a portfolio epithet (distinct per power; framed as the hell-host): Maraxus -> Marach the War-Fire (AS Mearox); Vacidus -> Wachid the Unmaker; Lusanto -> Lusando the Hoard-Worm.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Munstar (minster) of [power]: 'the Munstar of Dulro' (the AS shires keep an older Hearg-turned-minster).
religion.saints_pattern: Wih/Halig [name] (the holy [name]); the hallowed dead and royal saints venerated at the minster.

holy_symbol_motifs.Dulro: a sun-cross above the scales of judgment
holy_symbol_motifs.Erlant: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring

banks_patterns.ships: river-trader and saint names: 'the Saint Dulro', 'Swan of the Ost-Aha'
banks_patterns.military_units: the [lineage] Leudes / the [shire] Fyrd (AS overlay): 'the East-Fyrd', 'the Iron Lances of Ostraclia'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: ruined phalanza-palaces and old heargs gone to ruin: 'the broken Burg of [name]', 'the Sunken Munstar'
